items.title: Red September Pattern: Bitcoin and Wall Street's Seasonal Curse
points: Bitcoin closed lower in 8 of 13 completed Septembers since 2013, though there is no clear cause tied to crypto-specific cycles.
The S&P 500 has shown the same 'Red September' effect since 1945, suggesting broad market psychology rather than asset-specific factors.
Bitcoin started September 2026 near $77,000, down from an intraweek high above $80,000, despite posting its best August since 2021 with a 25% gain.

items.title: Tether Lawsuit Over Frozen USDT
points: Two Thai businessmen sued Tether over a $42.4 million freeze of USDT (Tether's US dollar-pegged stablecoin, a cryptocurrency designed to hold a steady $1 value) that happened months before U.S. federal authorities obtained a seizure warrant.
The suit raises questions about Tether's authority to unilaterally block user funds ahead of formal legal action.

items.title: SEC Proposes Transfer Agent Overhaul Citing Tokenization
points: The SEC proposed Form TA-2, requiring transfer agents (firms that maintain official records of who owns a company's shares) to disclose how many share registers they keep on distributed ledgers (blockchain-based record-keeping systems).
This is the first major overhaul of transfer agent rules in 40 years, reflecting growing regulatory attention to tokenized assets (real-world assets like stocks represented as blockchain tokens).

items.title: Robinhood Chain Growth and Adoption Surge
points: Robinhood Chain, an Ethereum layer-2 network (a secondary blockchain that processes transactions faster/cheaper before settling on Ethereum's main chain), hit $1.6 billion in decentralized exchange (DEX, a crypto trading platform with no central operator) trading volume.
Volume rose 61% in just days, with DeFi (decentralized finance, blockchain-based financial services without traditional intermediaries) deposits and stablecoin holdings nearing $800 million.
